両.meaning: Inside a <part>frame</part> under a <part>one</part>-plank top, a tiny <part>mountain</part> is split into two peaks, left and right. You can't climb just one. You have to conquer <kanji>both</kanji>.
両.on: Between the two peaks sits a <sound>ryo</sound>kan, a Japanese inn, where climbers rest.
両.kun: The innkeeper wants everyone to know: '<sound>Te</sound>ll both peaks, <sound>Roo</sound>!' he tells his pet kangaroo.

弁.meaning: An <part>elbow</part> juts up behind a football <part>goal</part>, where a plumber kneels gripping a pipe. He twists, the elbow strains, and with a squeak it finally turns. Hiss: the pitch sprinklers stop. It was a stuck <kanji>valve</kanji>.
弁.on: When it's done, the valve handle is <sound>ben</sound>t from all that twisting.
弁.kun: The plumber drops his key down the drain: '<sound>Wah</sound>! <sound>Key</sound>! <sound>Ma</sound>!' he wails, and his dog Roo answers '<sound>Eh</sound>? <sound>Roo</sound>!' Hush now: know what's proper.

辛.meaning: A pepper <part>stand</part> sells chilies under a sign: <part>ten</part> out of ten heat. Bite one and you leap up as if you'd stood on a nail. Hot, hot, <kanji>spicy</kanji>!
辛.on: Leaping around, you kick the chili stand and bang your <sound>shin</sound> on it.
辛.kun: Your mouth is on fire, so you dunk your face in the <sound>ca</sound>rp pond while a cheerleader shouts '<sound>Rah</sound>-rah!'

親.meaning: Someone balances on a <part>stand</part> at the top of a <part>tree</part>, face red from shouting 'Careful!', watching the playground through a zoomed-in <part>camera</part>. They never lose sight of one kid. That's a <kanji>parent</kanji>.
親.on: Through the camera they see their kid kick another kid's <sound>shin</sound>.
親.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>, <sound>yah</sound>, I saw that,' the parent calls down from the top of the tree.

苦.meaning: An <part>old</part> goat with no teeth left is made to chew ten bitter handfuls of <part>grass</part>, one after another. It gags on the third. By the tenth it is pure <kanji>suffering</kanji>.
苦.on: A <sound>cu</sound>ckoo pops out of its clock to count each handful.
苦.kun: A kangaroo hops in to help eat the grass, and the cuckoo cheers '<sound>Ku</sound>! <sound>Roo</sound>!'

落.meaning: <part>Grass</part> on the roof sheds <part>water drops</part> onto a row of folding chairs, soaking <part>each</part> one in turn. A man sits on the last, staring at the sky, and the wet chair snaps shut under him. Down he goes: a <kanji>fall</kanji>.
落.on: A heavy <sound>ruck</sound>sack falls off the roof right after him and lands on his chest.
落.kun: Flat on his back with a rucksack on top, he moans '<sound>Oh</sound>… <sound>chee</sound>se… <sound>roo</sound>!' as a kangaroo hops over him.
